result.summary: This is a fork of wk8/go-ordered-map: a generic insertion-ordered map with JSON (via encoding/json and buger/jsonparser) and YAML (go.yaml.in/yaml/v4) marshalling. I read all three files and found no init functions, build-time code, network, file, exec or environment access, encoded payloads, or runtime patching. The flagged capabilities come from reflection and interface-based serialization only.

findings.title: Minor correctness quirks in YAML handling
findings.detail: MarshalYAML returns []byte("null") for a nil map, which encodes as a byte sequence rather than a YAML null. UnmarshalYAML indexes Content[index+1] without checking bounds. These are ordinary bugs inherited from the wk8/go-ordered-map fork and have no security impact.

capabilities.explanation: This comes from reflection in MarshalJSON/UnmarshalJSON (reflect.ValueOf, Convert, Set) used to handle wrapper key types, and from calls through interfaces (json.Marshal, yaml Encode/Decode, TextMarshaler/TextUnmarshaler) that may invoke user-defined marshal methods. This is ordinary serialization behaviour, not dynamic code loading.

No network calls are present. The capability is most likely attributed transitively through encoding/json or yaml marshalling paths that can reach interface methods, for example the MarshalText/MarshalJSON of net types. The package itself only serializes and deserializes data in memory.
